shiba: Production pixel-art sprite sheet for a warm illustrated pet-shop game. Create one landscape transparent PNG, 3 columns by 4 rows, exactly 12 separated individual Shiba Inu dog sprites. Image 1 is the officially approved catalogue for the exact 12 individual coats and sex-specific silhouettes. Image 2 demonstrates the low, peaceful side-lying body pose and existing game's modest pixel-art rendering. For every cell from image 1 re-draw the same individual in lateral repose, head toward left and hindquarters toward right: closed eyelid visible, cheek and chin physically supported on ground, shoulder relaxed sideways, chest low, front paws limp and folded along floor, hind limbs fully folded at right. Genuine repose. foxlike wedge head, small upright triangular ears, compact coat, a thick curled plume resting at the rump, white urajiro areas. All dogs sideways, comparable sprite size, one dog per cell, a clear broad margin of transparent pixels in each cell. Use warm dark brown outlines, clean square pixel clusters and small highlight ramps, compatible with an 80 × 36px in-game size. Species proportions and distinctive markings matter. Output layout EXACT: row 1 covers female coats 1,2,3 left-to-right; row 2 female coats 4,5,6. Row 3 male coats 1,2,3; row 4 male coats 4,5,6. Six coat designs in the same order as reference: red with white lower face and chest; black-and-tan with tan eyebrows/muzzle; cream white; red sesame with peppered dark saddle on red; black sesame smoky gray-brown saddle and pale underside; white body with distinct red piebald patches. Male dogs have slightly broader cheek/chest and stronger shoulder than females; each remains visibly its own drawing with subtle pose differences. Draw the entire body including paws, ears and tail within each cell. Flat unlit transparency A=0 between all dogs. Exclude labels, numbers, typography, printed grid, lines, accessories, stars, props, bed, cast shadow, glow, floor or ground marks. No gore, no motion, no standing. Use all twelve equally spaced invisible cells; use left-facing natural horizontal repose for every dog.
